title: Two Dockerfiles: Separating Local Dev From CI for Playwright
excerpt: Keeping separate Dockerfiles for local development and CI/CD turned out to be one of the simplest, most valuable decisions in dockerizing a Playwright project.
html:
Not every improvement in a test automation framework comes from writing more test code. Sometimes, it comes from how the development environment is structured.

One approach that I found particularly valuable while dockerizing a Playwright test automation project was keeping separate Dockerfiles for local development and CI/CD.

A Dockerfile.dev can be tailored for development by keeping the container alive for debugging, interactive testing, and iterative changes without constantly rebuilding the environment.

A separate Dockerfile for CI/CD, on the other hand, focuses on building a clean, reproducible image that executes the test suite and exits. This keeps pipeline execution predictable and avoids carrying development-specific configurations into automated workflows.

For the project, separating the two environments meant each Dockerfile could focus on a single responsibility: one optimized for development, the other for automated execution. The result was a setup that felt cleaner, easier to maintain, and simpler to evolve as the project grows.

Sometimes, the biggest improvements in an automation framework come from thoughtful engineering decisions behind the scenes rather than the test code itself.
